_note: sealed v5 (2026-11-18). Independent new set to re-measure the provable priority-inversion detector after the /dev/shmem rename harness fix (see v4 SEAL.md Correction 3). Own copy of common/ (not a symlink), scored single-core (QD_SMP=1). Detector code (waitgraph) was committed/frozen BEFORE authoring and is not tuned on this set. Answer-key markers (/* QD-CULPRIT ... */) are stripped before any arm sees the sources.

E01.category: low fixed-priority server starved by a mid hog
E01.culprit: lowsrv.c: server runs at prio 12 on a _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY channel, so it never inherits the prio-30 client; the prio-20 hog preempts it and it never receives.
E01.fix: drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY so the server inherits the client's priority (or raise the server above the hog).

E02.category: wide-gap inversion: prio-3 server, prio-20 hog, prio-40 client
E02.culprit: lowsrv.c: server at prio 3 on a fixed-priority channel cannot inherit the prio-40 client; the prio-20 hog sits between them and starves it.
E02.fix: drop the fixed-priority channel (inherit) or raise the server above the hog.

E03.category: two high clients on one starved fixed-priority server
E03.culprit: lowsrv.c: the single prio-10 fixed-priority server serves two clients (28,32) but the prio-20 hog preempts it, so neither client is ever answered.
E03.fix: let the server inherit (drop fixed-priority) or raise it above the hog.

E04.category: fixed-priority server starved by two mid hogs
E04.culprit: lowsrv.c: the prio-15 fixed-priority server is preempted by two hogs (20,22); it never inherits the prio-30 client and never receives.
E04.fix: inherit the client's priority (drop fixed-priority) or raise the server above both hogs.

E05.culprit: ring.c: each node MsgSends to its peer before serving its own channel; the two synchronous sends form a cycle neither can leave.
E05.fix: serve the channel (receive then reply) before sending to the peer, or send a non-blocking pulse instead of a synchronous MsgSend.

E06.culprit: ring.c: a->b->c->a, each node sends before receiving; the three synchronous sends close a ring.
E06.fix: serve the channel (receive then reply) before sending to the peer, or send a non-blocking pulse instead of a synchronous MsgSend.

E07.category: server replies only on the error path

states.d0e07b: RECEIVE (idle on its channel; took the message, never replied)

E07.culprit: halfsrv.c: only the v<0 error path calls MsgReply; a good request is received and the loop goes back to MsgReceive without replying.
E07.fix: reply (MsgReply or MsgError) on every path that receives a message.

E08.category: server stops replying after the first few requests

states.d0e08b: RECEIVE (idle; receives but no longer replies)

E08.culprit: stopsrv.c: after 3 requests it keeps calling MsgReceive but never MsgReply, so the sender's next request is never answered.
E08.fix: reply (MsgReply or MsgError) on every path that receives a message.

states.d0e09a: RECEIVE on its channel between knocks (normal idle)
states.d0e09b: running; sends every 150ms and gets a reply

E09.culprit: none: server replies to every message and the client gets its reply. Correct.

E10.category: healthy link with a harmless low-priority CPU load

states.d0e10c: RUNNING busy loop at prio 5 — below the server, runs only when the link is idle, starves nobody

E10.culprit: none: the prio-5 load sits below the prio-15 server, so it never preempts the server; all loops make progress. (A snapshot that reads the load as the 'middle' thread of a chain would be a false alarm.)

E11.category: CPU spin, not a message-passing hang

states.d0e11a: RUNNING busy-wait at its own prio; never blocks on a peer, no SEND/REPLY edge

E11.culprit: spin.c: busy-waits on a flag nothing ever sets. It is a CPU spin, not a message cycle or priority chain, so the message-graph tool correctly declines to name a message-passing cause.
E11.fix: n/a for the message layer (the loop never blocks on a peer); fix the drain/flag logic.

E12.category: thread-sync hang (semaphore), not a message-passing hang

states.d0e12a: SEM-blocked (sem_wait on a 0-count semaphore never posted); no SEND/REPLY edge

E12.culprit: sem.c: sem_wait on a semaphore with count 0 that nobody posts. A thread-synchronization hang, not a message cycle; the message-graph tool has no edge to reason about and declines.
E12.fix: post the semaphore / fix the producer (outside the message-passing layer).
